A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robustness study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplements are readable and can be matched reliably, including renumbered sections and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original adversarial evaluations across classification, transfer learning, segmentation, and detection, together with ablations and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet adversarial results for DINOv2-S, DINOv2-B, and MAE in supplementary Table 12.

M1.justification: The attack procedures and existing adaptations for vision transformers are unchanged. DINOv2 and MAE are additional evaluated models, not new algorithms or modifications proposed by this work.

E1.justification: The added DINOv2 checkpoints introduce pretraining on the separate, over-140-million-image dataset described in new supplementary Section 2, beyond the earlier ImageNet-pretrained model pool. The actual evaluation datasets and tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Supplementary Table 12 adds DINOv2-S, DINOv2-B, and MAE to the ImageNet model comparison. Existing comparator sets in the other experiments are retained, making this a limited expansion.

E3.justification: The additional ImageNet comparison includes small/base DINOv2 and base MAE configurations. Supplementary Section 2 describes distilled DINOv2 variants and partial fine-tuning for MAE, introducing heterogeneous settings relative to linear probing. Existing attack hyperparameters, metrics, and evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The MoCo-version, BYOL augmentation/batch-size, training-duration, backbone-architecture, regression, and feature-space analyses are retained. The new model table extends benchmarking without adding a controlled ablation or separate robustness-analysis procedure.

E5.justification: The 95% regression confidence bands in Figures 1–2 are retained. No repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practices are introduced.

E6.justification: New supplementary Table 12 reports per-attack results and overall adversarial averages of 34.87, 44.25, and 43.91 for DINOv2-S, DINOv2-B, and MAE, respectively. These are additional model results, not same-setting performance improvements. All retained appendix result tables preserve their numerical contents.

T1.justification: The Direction Ratio and Magnitude Ratio definitions, mathematical descriptions of attacks, and regression formulations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The introduction adds the finding that DINOv2 and MAE do not exhibit consistently high or low robustness. The abstract and central conclusions about SSL, downstream transfer, architecture, and training duration retain their substantive scope.

C2.justification: New supplementary Section 2 qualifies comparisons involving DINOv2’s much larger pretraining dataset and distilled variants, and MAE’s partial fine-tuning rather than pure linear probing. These add concrete comparability limitations; earlier mechanism explanations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: New supplementary Section 3 supplies model-repository links, identifies Torchattacks for instance attacks, and attributes the UAP implementation source. Conversely, the shortened Section 3.1 removes explicit backbone parameter-count and pretraining sample-count details. This changes documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same cited works, including DINOv2 and MAE. The added closing paragraph in Related Work reiterates the broad cross-model, multi-task positioning already stated in v1’s introduction.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the model setup and conclusion, adds acknowledgements and two supplementary sections, and makes local wording edits. The overall narrative structure remains. Numerous main-text supplement references retain obsolete section numbers after the additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds supplementary Table 12, resizes Figures 1–2, and relocates Table 3 while rearranging the surrounding appendix layout. Existing figure content and retained table structures are preserved; subsequent tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The additional model comparisons, explicit comparability caveats, and repository links offer useful gains. However, new Table 12 contains unexplained UAP-average inconsistencies: MAE’s 16 listed UAP scores average 46.33, whereas the reported UAP average is 43.61. Appendix renumbering also leaves many main-text references stale. These reporting problems undermine the principal new evidence and navigation, so the benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
